From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme — latency/throughput benchmarks

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Per Marissa's note, we ran the baseline on a representative subset of the prompt set you shared. High-level results (single-request, cold KV cache unless noted):

- Model variant: open-llm-v1-medium (quantized FP16 path) on p4d-equivalent instance
- Prompt length: 512 tokens input, 128 tokens generation
- p50 latency: ~110 ms
- p95 latency: ~360 ms
- Throughput: ~42 tokens/sec sustained for steady-state batched requests (batch size 4)
- Notes: with prefix/KV cache warmed, p95 improved to ~280 ms for repeat traffic patterns; batching to 8 gives ~1.7x throughput gain but increases p95 by ~40-70 ms depending on concurrency.

Attached is the raw benchmark PDF and the config we used (batching, kv cache, and quantization flags). These numbers come from our internal optimized runtime; your mileage may vary depending on networking and exact instance type. If you want, we can re-run these on a region/instance that matches your setup.

[Attachment: redwood-latency-benchmarks.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: acme-test-config.txt (text, 3KB)]

If helpful, I can also share a short perf dashboard link with the full trace.

- Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
